articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Native Multimodal Reasoning and Extended Context
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5 in early May 2026, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning across text, image, audio, and video inputs with a context window exceeding 1 million tokens. The model demonstrates significant improvements in long-horizon planning tasks and mathematical proof generation, narrowing the gap with domain-specific systems. Enterprise API availability rolled out with tiered pricing based on context utilization.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Graduate-Level Science Benchmarks
articles.summary: DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 set new records on GPQA Diamond and several graduate-level STEM benchmarks, surpassing 80% accuracy on PhD-qualifier-level physics and chemistry problems. The model leverages a new mixture-of-experts architecture with specialized science reasoning heads trained on curated datasets of peer-reviewed literature. Researchers note this marks a meaningful step toward AI-assisted scientific discovery workflows.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in Automotive Manufacturing Lines
articles.summary: Tesla announced that its third-generation Optimus humanoid robot has entered limited production deployment at its Austin Gigafactory, performing repetitive assembly tasks alongside human workers. The Gen 3 units feature improved dexterous manipulation with 22 degrees of freedom per hand and onboard vision-language models for natural-language task instruction. Tesla plans broader external sales to manufacturing partners by Q4 2026.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Atlas Commercial Platform for Construction Sites
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics, backed by Hyundai, revealed the commercial version of its electric Atlas humanoid robot purpose-built for construction environments, featuring IP67 dust and water resistance and the ability to carry 50 kg payloads across uneven terrain. The platform integrates a digital-twin planning system that lets operators choreograph multi-robot workflows from a single interface. Pilot deployments are underway with three major construction firms in South Korea and the United States.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Tool-Use Agents with Persistent Memory and Autonomous Task Execution
articles.summary: Anthropic released a major update to its Claude model family enabling persistent memory across sessions and autonomous multi-step tool-use agents that can execute complex workflows over hours without human intervention. The system includes a novel constitutional-AI-based guardrail layer that continuously audits agent actions against user-defined safety policies. Early adopters report 40-60% reductions in time spent on repetitive software engineering and data analysis pipelines.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Gate-All-Around Process Node
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed that its A14 (1.4nm-class) process using gate-all-around nanosheet transistors has entered volume production at its Fab 20 complex in Tainan, with Apple and Nvidia as lead customers. The node delivers an estimated 20% speed improvement and 30% power reduction over N2, critical for next-generation AI accelerator chips. This cements TSMC's manufacturing lead as Intel and Samsung continue ramping their competing 14A and SF1.4 nodes.

articles.title: Microsoft and Quantinuum Demonstrate Fault-Tolerant Logical Qubit Operations Below Error Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Quantinuum jointly announced sustained fault-tolerant operations on 12 logical qubits with error rates below the threshold required for practical quantum error correction, using Quantinuum's H3 trapped-ion processor and Microsoft's topological error-correction codes. This milestone is considered a critical prerequisite for scaling to the hundreds of logical qubits needed for commercially relevant quantum algorithms. The team published a roadmap targeting a 100-logical-qubit system by late 2027.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Phase Begins with First Compliance Audits of Foundation Model Providers
articles.summary: The European AI Office initiated its first formal compliance audits under the EU AI Act's general-purpose AI provisions, targeting major foundation model providers including OpenAI, Google, and Meta to assess adherence to transparency, safety testing, and energy reporting requirements. Companies face potential fines of up to 3% of global revenue for non-compliance. The enforcement action is being closely watched as a bellwether for global AI regulation and has prompted several providers to publish detailed model cards and systemic risk assessments.
